messages:
sarah: Quick heads-up — I ran a replay harness (toolcall-heavy, JSON mode on) vs synthetic traffic and we see a ~18% p95 latency regression when the kernel selector flips to the int8-optimized matmul on A100. Anyone else seeing toolcall/JSON overhead spike when kernel changes?

mike: @sarah can you paste the exact harness command and the kernel selection logs? Also was KV cache warm?

sarah: Command: `./replay_harness --trace=fuzzer_trace.json --qps=1200 --json-mode=true --batch-window-ms=8 --kernel-policy=auto`
Logs excerpt: ```[2026-03-01T14:12:03Z] kernel_selector: chosen=matmul_int8_opt, fallback=matmul_fp16
[2026-03-01T14:12:03Z] runtime: admit_latency_ms=3.2, batch_size=12
[2026-03-01T14:12:03Z] kvcache: hit_rate=0.67, eviction=LRU, active_entries=28712```

vivek: Interesting — toolcall JSON validation forces a full decode/serialize step for responses, which can blow up per-request CPU. If the kernel swaps to int8 path we might be seeing CPU-GPU sync cost + extra memcpy. Do you have perf profile?

jen: Attached sampling profile (top lines). Note the spike in `json_validate()` and `pybind_serialize()` around the same time kernel changes. Also noticed several validation failures that triggered retries: ```{"request_id":"r-9a1","error":"json_validation:trailing_comma","attempts":2}```

perf-bot: benchmark-summary: replay=toolcall-heavy json-mode ON qps=1200 p50=28ms p95=142ms p99=310ms cost_per_1k_tokens=0.92USD. Synthetic-same-seed: p95=120ms. Relative p95 regression=18.3%.

mike: Are we comparing apples-to-apples? Did you pin model version + batch window? Synthetic tests sometimes use smaller sequences.

sarah: Yes pinned model to v2.3.4 and seeds same. The one difference is warm vs cold KV cache: I reran with warm-cache primed (same trace warm-run) => p95 improves ~6% but still >10% regression vs synthetic.

vivek: Two hypotheses: 1) kernel change reduces single-op latency but increases variability for certain sequence-length mixes (affects batching heuristics). 2) JSON validation path runs on CPU threadpool; if serialization blocks, we lose batching opportunities and see head-of-line latency spikes.

jen: Repro steps I used: ```# warm priming
./replay_harness --trace=fuzzer_trace.json --qps=200 --duration=30s --warm
# test
./replay_harness --trace=fuzzer_trace.json --qps=1200 --duration=120s --json-mode=true --batch-window-ms=8 --kernel-policy=auto
```
I also tried forcing kernel `matmul_fp16` via `--kernel-policy=pin:matmul_fp16` and p95 dropped back to ~122ms.

mike: That pin experiment is telling. Can you run experiment matrix: batch-window {4,8,16}, kernel-policy {auto,pin_fp16,pin_int8}, json-mode {on,off}, kvcache {cold,warm} and dump p95/p99? We need apples-to-apples table.

sarah: On it. I'll run overnight distributed matrix and upload results. Quick note: retries due to validation failures add ~2x cost on those requests and inflate p99 — we should surface retry counts per-route in the console.

vivek: Also add a microbenchmark: measure time spent in `json_validate()` vs `pybind_serialize()` and time between GPU-kernel completion and user-visible send (to detect memcpy/sync). If memcpy is the culprit we can try pinned host buffers or streaming serialize to avoid full copy.

jen: I saw one regression trace where batching window increased dynamically because runtime thought longer sequences would fit — but because CPU was blocked on validation, admitted batches were smaller and latency rose. Suggest adding a metric: percent-time-epochs-where-json-queue-length>threshold.

perf-bot: scheduled-job: sarah run matrix -> results uploaded to /benchmarks/replays/1767512345/matrix.csv by 2026-03-02T06:00Z

sarah: Filing a short RFC for a mitigation: 1) opportunistic offload JSON validation to background thread or gpu-accel (if available), 2) make kernel selector cost-aware of CPU-side postprocessing, and 3) default batch-window to 6ms for toolcall-heavy routes. Will post RFC draft.

mike: Thanks — please @me on RFC. If matrix shows pin_fp16 fixes most regressions we should consider temporarily pinning for hosted until we have offload.

sarah: Will do. Running matrix now, will report numbers + CSV link once complete. :rocket:
